newsitem.title: THAILAND: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Oct 2.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Oct 2.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Thai press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Gen Chavalit Yongchaiyudh's hopes of becoming prime minister have been enhanced when Chart Thai secretary-general Snoh Thienthong and almost all incumbent Nam Thai members of parliament announced that they will contest the November general election under his New Aspiration party's banner. (BANGKOK POST) (THE NATION)
- Bangkok has been hit by the most serious flooding in recent months following heavy downpours early on Tuesday that also resulted in traffic chaos on many major roads. (THE NATION)

- More than 50 pet shops are selling thousands of iguanas, both retail and wholesale, at a Bangkok market. One shop owner says he imports some 1,000 of them from El Salvador and Guatemala each month. (BANGKOK POST)

- The Airport Authority of Thailand (AAT) will increase Bangkok International Airport's handling capacity from 23 million to 37 million passengers a year by 2003 in preparation for a two-year delay in opening the new airport at Bangkok's outskirts of Nong Ngu Hao. (THE NATION)

- The Bank of Thailand is considering contributing 340 million special drawing rights (worth US$476 million) to the International Monetary Fund's emergency fund, called the "New Arrangement to Borrow". (THE NATION)

- Screening of costly state projects will be stepped up to avert meddling by politicians. From December 1, all investment planned by state agencies and enterprises must be checked by the National Economic and Social Development Board before it can be approved. (BANGKOK POST)
